items.quote: The king sent a messenger ahead, but before he arrived, Elisha said to the elders, “Don’t you see how this murderer is sending someone to cut off my head?
items.contrast: The reader must distinguish the king, who sends the threat, from the messenger he sends.
items.reason: The messenger is a plausible alternative because he comes to Elisha, but Elisha calls the person who is “sending someone” the murderer. The preceding sentence identifies that sender as the king, so the key is uniquely supported and the wording clearly asks for the title’s referent.
